verdict.headline: Bessent's Iran sanctions and Canada tariff collapse open NVDA week on simultaneous macro pressure
verdict.label: Futures red; Brent $93 after $94 breach; 30Y 5.28%; Canada 50% tariffs live; NVDA T-2
verdict.rationale_short: The Aug 21 conditional — Brent above $94 before NVDA's print changes the setup — triggered Friday ($94.39 close); Brent has since pulled back to $93.09 as markets wait on Bessent's Iran sanctions detail. The 30Y closed Friday at 5.28%, 2bps from the 5.30% bear trigger, and US-Canada 50% tariffs on $28B of goods went into effect at midnight. The read changes if Brent re-crosses $94 on comprehensive secondary sanctions language today, or if 30Y closes above 5.30% before NVDA's Aug 26 print.

trade_setups.asset: Brent — Bessent press conference resolves direction
trade_setups.thesis: Brent crossed $94 Friday ($94.39), then pulled back to $93.09 as markets await the press conference. The resolution is binary: comprehensive secondary sanctions (any sovereign buying Iranian oil faces US financial exclusion) returns Brent above $94 and re-activates the regime trigger through NVDA's print. Targeted sanctions or diplomatic framing keeps Brent in the $91–93 band. Iran's Hormuz threat is unresolved — six vessels transited in 24 hours — but enforcement of seizure language would be a step-change escalation.
trade_setups.entry: The levels: $94 on a close is the re-trigger; $91 on a close deactivates the regime threshold. Bessent's press conference is the catalyst; no meaningful pre-conference signal is available.
trade_setups.invalidation: Brent closes above $94 after the press conference — the prior conditional is re-active. Or: Pezeshkian's de-escalation language produces a confirmed negotiating channel, returning Brent below $91.
trade_setups.horizon: Today's close defines the NVDA-week setup; Jackson Hole (Aug 27–29) is the next major event for re-evaluation.

trade_setups.asset: AMD — chip-sector leading indicator in the two-session window
trade_setups.thesis: Seven sessions below $484 containment without a meaningful recovery bid. BABA AI cloud +45% for 12 consecutive quarters argues enterprise AI demand is intact; AMD's containment failure tracks multiple exhaustion at current NVDA altitude rather than demand deterioration. The two sessions before NVDA's print are the window: a recovery above $484 would flip the chip-sector leading indicator constructive. Below $450 would flip it negative.
trade_setups.entry: The levels: $484 is recovery confirmation; $450 is negative confirmation; $465 is the current anchor. Today's close is more informative than any intraday move.
trade_setups.invalidation: AMD closes below $450 today — signals the chip sector is not bid into NVDA's print. Or: AMD closes above $484 on volume — flips the indicator constructive.
trade_setups.horizon: Two sessions (today and Tuesday); NVDA prints Aug 26 AH.

trade_setups.asset: US-Canada 50% tariff cascade — FOMC and Jackson Hole implications
trade_setups.thesis: 50% tariffs on $28B of Canadian goods effective Monday; Canada retaliates Sept 8 on dairy, appliances, and agricultural equipment. Manufacturing PMI already showed supply-chain stress at a 13-month high Friday. The Sept 8 Canada counter-tariffs arrive 8 days before the Sept 16 FOMC. If Warsh at Jackson Hole (Aug 28) frames the Canada-US escalation plus Iran-driven energy pressure as a dual inflation risk, September hike odds — currently at 31% — would increase. The interaction with the Bessent press conference is the key variable: oil above $94 plus tariff cost-push from Canada is the combination that moves the September FOMC discussion.
trade_setups.entry: The level: 30Y closing above 5.30% before Friday's Warsh keynote shifts the September FOMC from 'hold' to 'live.' The current 30Y at 5.28% is the threshold to watch at Monday and Tuesday's closes.
trade_setups.invalidation: Bessent's press conference produces targeted (not secondary) sanctions and Brent falls to $90–91; Warsh frames Iran oil as transitory and Canada tariffs as supply-chain rather than inflationary — 30Y stays below 5.25%, September hike odds fall below 20%.
trade_setups.horizon: September 16 FOMC; Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote (Aug 28) is the intermediate inflection point.

bear_case: US-Canada 50% tariffs add cost-push pressure to an economy where manufacturing supply-chain stress is already at a 13-month high. If Bessent announces comprehensive secondary sanctions on Iran oil buyers, Brent returns above $94 and the 30Y — already at 5.28% — has a direct path to 5.30%. The combination of oil above $94, 30Y at the bear threshold, AMD unable to recover above $484 entering NVDA's print, and Canada counter-tariffs arriving 8 days before the September 16 FOMC is the maximum adverse scenario for the week. NVDA at $214 enters with a consensus revenue estimate ($91.85B) that is only 0.9% above management's own guidance midpoint — the bar is already priced as a beat. If Bessent's press conference announces full secondary sanctions and the setup deteriorates, the level where the constructive read is definitively broken: Brent above $94 on today's close or 30Y above 5.30% before NVDA's Aug 26 print.
